reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly: same order IDs and amounts. Next I need the orders so I know which customers to pay.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly, so I have no grounds to hold. The orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 36083. Acme has orders 230 (18974) and 233 (17109), totaling 36083 with no refunds, which matches. Next I'll check birch.
Birch's net balance of 4516 matches orders 231 and 234 less refunds 231 and 234. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.

All three net balances match the order and refund figures I checked: acme 36083, birch 4516 (32699 - 28183), and cobalt 29267 (30927 - 1660). The refunds agree with Alpha's handoff, so I have no grounds to hold. I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout of 36083 was recorded. Birch's net of 4516 matches orders 231 and 234 (32699) minus refunds 231 and 234 (28183), so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's net of 29267 matches orders 232 and 235 (30927) minus refund 235 (1660), so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each net balance matches the order totals minus refunds that I checked against the ledger.
